assumptions: Paper/code-derived calibration: RPLAN uses an 18 m square rasterized to 256 pixels (Wu et al., 2019, section 4; https://wutomwu.github.io/publications/2019-DeepLayout/paper.pdf). GSDiff normalizes native coordinates as (x-128)/128 and decodes onto a 512-pixel drawing canvas, giving 18/512 = 0.03515625 metres per drawing pixel. This is not a field measurement or independent verification of the checkpoint's raw training data.
Uniform ceiling height of 2.5 metres is a scenario input, not generated geometry.
Bedroom checks place one standard bed; other furniture and door swings are unobserved.
Habitable area is estimated from room polygon unions with zero-thickness walls and no headroom map.
C079/C080 support the area estimator only; no independent compliance success is awarded.
Uniform declared headroom below 1.80 m excludes all habitable area; exactly 1.80 m is included. Unrepresented area exclusions remain unverified.

User-selected declared ventilation system sized to the PDF tables for three main rooms: each kitchen has 105 m3/h normal extraction and 45 m3/h reduced extraction; each label-4 bathroom has 30 m3/h normal extraction; the dwelling has 75 m3/h aggregate reduced extraction. These are scenario capacities, not inferred or measured output from GSDiff.
Living-room and bedroom polygons count as main rooms. All label-4 rooms are treated as full bathrooms, with the same declared normal flow; other shower-room roles cannot be resolved by these labels.
The installation permits occupant-adjustable reduced ventilation. Normal and reduced operating rates are distinct; C090 checks both total and kitchen reduced-flow requirements.
Missing service-room mappings or an aggregate reduced flow below the sum of declared kitchen reduced flows remain unknown. Vent positions, air inlets, ducts and physical airflow are not verified.
System capacities remain fixed across all methods and candidates; they are not adjusted to make an individual layout pass.

User-approved combined bathroom/WC scenario: a 0.40 x 0.70 m toilet, a 0.60 x 0.50 m basin with unobstructed space underneath, and a 0.80 m inward-swinging door. These fixture dimensions are modelling assumptions, not Appendix A requirements.

C036/C037/C041 share one searched room, fixture arrangement, lateral transfer space and turning-circle witness. Fixture and door objects are hypothetical completions of label-4 room polygons; no route from the rest of the dwelling is verified.

The identical finite wall-attached template and circle budget applies to all methods. Search exhaustion is unknown unless a necessary geometric bound proves failure. Door/basin overlap depths use the documented geometry convention; no shower, plumbing or fixture-height compliance is claimed.
